column4: Same dark starry background and horizontal framing as the first reference. The living librarian's hand (from the left, natural skin, white blouse cuff with a black button) and the porcelain doll's hand (from the right, ivory porcelain with ball joints, brass wrist ring and ruffled black cuff) are now clasped firmly together at the center of the frame, palm to palm, fingers wrapped around each other, a steady, comforting hold. Exactly five fingers visible per hand. No threads, no strings, no text.

Identical locked camera, cathedral nave, doors and floor as the first reference, but the right-hand door has been pushed open a little wider, so the bright ivory strip of light between the doors is wider than before. The new small porcelain maid doll (third reference: long orange hair, orange flower ornament, black dress with white apron, white boots, ball joints) stands at the gap seen from behind and slightly from the side, her head tilted forward to peek out through the opening, one porcelain hand resting on the edge of the open door. She is small, about one third of the door's height. The light stays flat ivory, no other color. No strings, no text.
